CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, MARCH 24, 2026

CALL TO ORDER  Joshua Barron, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to order at
  6:50 p.m.

INVOCATION  Tina De La Rosa, Acting Director of Parks & Recreation
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE  Manuel Arana, Chief of Police

ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor Joshua Barron, Vice Mayor Al Rios, Council Member Maria del
  Pilar Avalos, Council Member Gil Hurtado, and Council Member Maria
  Davila; City Treasurer Jose De La Paz, City Manager Rob Houston, City
  Attorney Raúl F. Salinas

PUBLIC HEARINGS

1
MUNICIPAL CODE
ADMIN  Following the conclusion of the Public Hearing, the City Council
  unanimously approved (as amended) items A & B by motion of Vice
  Mayor Rios and seconded by Council Member Hurtado:

  a. Introduced Ordinance No. 2026-02-CC entitled Ordinance of the City
  Council of the City of South Gate, California, amending Title 7 (Public
  Safety and Morals), of Chapter 7.49 (Park), Section 7.49.150 (Curfew)
  by modifying Subsection 7.49.150(B) and adding Subsections
  7.49.150(C) (Extended Park Hours) and 7.49.150(D) (Park Closure) to
  the South Gate Municipal Code relating to curfews in City of South
  Gate municipal parks to allow for permitted activities in parks without
  buildings beyond sunset and to provide the City Manager flexibility to
  amend park hours by administrative action citywide; and

  b. Finding that this action is exempt from the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to the General Rule Exemption under
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3), as there is no possibility that
  the ordinance amendment may have a significant effect on the
  environment, and as a Class 1 Categorical Exemption under CEQA
  Guidelines Section 15301 (Existing Facilities), as the amendment
  involves only a minor change to the administrative hours of operation
  of existing park facilities with no physical alteration to the
  environment. The City Clerk is directed to file a Notice of Exemption
  with the County Clerk within five (5) working days of adoption.
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 24, 2026

1
MUNICIPAL CODE
ADMIN CONT’D  Tina De La Rosa, Acting Director of Parks & Recreation provided the
  presentation.

  Mayor Barron asked if anyone in the audience wished to speak on this
  item.

  Mario Dominguez, a South Gate resident, expressed opposition to granting
  the City Manager authority over city parks and recommended assigning
  this responsibility to either the Director of Parks and Recreation or the
  Chief of Police.

  Jimmy Ozaeta, a South Gate resident, expressed opposition to delegating
  authority to City Manager as proposed in the municipal code amendment.
  While acknowledging the City’s efforts to support Street Soccer USA
  programming, he stated concern with the mechanism proposed to achieve
  that objective. He added that the ordinance would allow the City Manager
  to unilaterally extend park hours at any city park, requiring only a written
  notice to the City Council within seven days after the decision.

  Mr. Ozaeta recommended several measures for consideration. He
  proposed requiring prior Council approval for any extension of city park
  hours, not only those past midnight. He also suggested implementing
  advance community notification to ensure affected residents are informed.
  In addition, he recommended adding an annual review clause to allow the
  Council to reassess the effectiveness and alignment of the ordinance. He
  further requested that any extension of hours include written justification
  to maintain transparency.

  Regarding park closures, he expressed support for extending emergency
  closure authority for recreation centers to the City Manager and Chief of
  Police when safety concerns arise. He emphasized that South Gate
  residents deserve parks that are safe, well managed, and responsive to
  community needs rather than administrative convenience.

  Edgar Pelayo, a South Gate resident, reiterated the concerns raised by
  previous speakers and noted that extending park hours could have fiscal
  implications.

  Robyn Logan, a South Gate resident, inquired whether the City Manager
  is responsible for any portion of the budget, including oversight of
  expenditures related to items such as lighting and security. Ms. Logan
  expressed the belief that the Chief of Police has ultimate authority in these
  matters and would be the appropriate official to inform the public about
  safety within any permissible area.

  Page 2 of 26
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 24, 2026

1
MUNICIPAL CODE
ADMIN CONT’D  Having no one else come forward, Mayor Barron closed the audience
  portion.

  Council Member Avalos heard the community concerns. She has some
  questions that have to do with the city ensuring adequate Council
  oversight for administrative decisions that are being made. Also including
  in that is hopefully making a quarterly report or quarterly presentation to
  let Council know under what circumstances will staff be seeking Council
  approval when closures come. She agrees when dealing with public safety,
  she would like to include not only the Chief of Police but also the
  department head of Parks and Rec be included.

  Council Member Avalos asked how residents will be notified of any
  extended hours or recurring events that are happening. What mitigation
  measures will be used for noise, lighting, and traffic impacts?

  Vice Mayor Rios knows the city has a few parks which triggered
  compliance for Street Soccer USA. As far as to the other parks, they are
  not going to be impacted by this code.

  Mr. Houston replied not at this time. The idea is that down the road if
  there was a decision to change some of the smaller parks, but not now due
  to budget and lack of staff. Street Soccer USA is putting up a facility at
  Hollydale Regional Park, being open seven days a week, installing
  lighting, and providing their own staff for security at no cost to the city.

  Council Member Hurtado asked if this issue was ever considered before
  the Parks Commission first and then to Council if needed.

  Mr. Houston stated that for the purposes of Street Soccer USA, the staff
  have been in a mad speed rush.

  Mayor Barron understands the goal is not to create a menace. The goal is
  to create an event where the community can come out and enjoy the park
  at an hour that is not normally used for. He questioned why this item has
  come before Council.

  Ms. De La Rosa stated the ordinance reads parks with buildings or
  structures which South Gate Park and Hollydale Community Park have
  buildings with structures and there is a 10:00 p.m. curfew time on those
  parks.

  Mayor Barron stated that in the past when we’ve had some emergencies at
  the parks the Chief of Police made the call to cancel events. He does not
  see anything being taken away based on this ordinance.

  Page 3 of 26
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 24, 2026

1
MUNICIPAL CODE
ADMIN CONT’D  Mr. Houston stated the Chief of Police consults with City Manager and
  then decides on closing the park. So, ultimately it is the City Manager’s
  choice.

  Council Member Avalos is requesting to include the Chief of Police and
  the Director of Parks & Recreation given the fact that Council is
  introducing an ordinance.

  Mr. Houston stated if that’s the requirement recommended, it could state
  the City Manager in consultation with the Parks & Rec Director, and
  Police Chief.

  Council Member Davila doesn’t see any issue authorizing the City
  Manager. She knows the City Manager, Chief of Police and Director of
  Parks & Recreation are always working together.

  Ms. De La Rosa stated that the specific language in the ordinance states
  propose a new subsection C delegates authority of City Manager or a duly
  authorized representative to extend park hours of operation beyond the
  standard curfew hours.

  Mayor Barron asked Councilwoman Avalos if she wants it specifically
  stated to a certain department.

  Council Member Avalos responded in the affirmative.

  AMENDMENT: include the phrase that says, “in consultation with
  appropriate staff.”

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Council Member Davila, yes; Vice Mayor Rios, yes; Mayor Barron,
  yes.

2
PARKING & TRAFFIC  Following the conclusion of the Public Hearing, the City Council
  approved items A, B, C & D by motion of Council Member Hurtado and
  second by Council Member Davila:

  a. Resolution No. 2026-11-CC entitled Resolution of the City Council of
  the City of South Gate, California, confirming the voting results for
  establishing a Preferential Parking District on Beaudine from 8813
  Beaudine Avenue to 8944 Beaudine Avenue to prohibit parking
  between the hours of 4:00 PM and 10:00 PM Monday to Friday except
  by permit; and

  Page 4 of 26
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 24, 2026

2
PARKING & TRAFFIC
CONT’D
  b. Directed the Public Works Department to install parking restriction
  signage within 90 days of the approval of the Resolution; and

  c. Directed the City Clerk to notify the property owners on Beaudine
  Avenue of March 5, 2026, voting results; and

  d. Appropriated $1,500 in Gas Tax Funds to install the parking
  restrictions.

  Mayor Barron recused himself from this item due to his residence on
  Beaudine Avenue.

  Arturo Cervantes, Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director, gave the
  presentation.

  Vice Mayor Rios asked if anyone in the audience wished to speak on this
  item.

  Selena Andrade lives on Beaudine Avenue, where parking restrictions are
  enforced. Residents frequently find unauthorized vehicles parked and call
  enforcement or police, but rarely get a response, especially at night. She
  asks how enforcement will work if the new item is approved. Selena notes
  the two-permit rule is insufficient for her family of six, including two
  college students and two high school students. Many neighbors support
  the petition, but there are concerns about fairness, as residents with
  handicap plaques also receive two permits, effectively getting three and
  creating inequality.

  She hoped Mayor Barron would be there since he owns several cars. Does
  he have a city permit plus two others, totaling three permits?

  Jimmy Ozaeta, a resident of South Gate, acknowledges the existence of a
  $1,500 allocation from gas tax funds. He inquires whether the city would
  consider investing these funds in permitting for every street if all residents
  chose to participate in the process, and requests information on alternative
  options available for the use of gas tax funds.

  Having no one else come forward, Mayor Barron closed the audience
  portion.
EMAILS  Julia expressed interest and in favor of having the preferential parking.

  Page 5 of 26
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 24, 2026

2
PARKING & TRAFFIC
CONT’D  Mr. Cervantes explained that the Council redesigned the Preferential
  Parking District Program approximately four to five years ago. At that
  time, the program allowed only one permit per property; however, this
  resulted in underutilized on-street parking. As a result, the program was
  revised to allow up to two permits per property, which reflects the
  maximum number of vehicles that can physically be accommodated on the
  street.

  The intent of the program is to discourage excessive on-street parking and
  encourage residents to use available garages and driveways, which most
  properties have. The program is not intended to accommodate four or six
  permits per property.

  Regarding the suggestion that the mayor may receive an additional permit
  due to his role as a city representative, Mr. Cervantes clarified that the
  program does not provide for a third permit under any circumstances.

  He further noted that ADA parking spaces are governed by a separate
  ordinance and are not subject to the Preferential Parking District Program.

  Finally, with respect to gas tax funding, Mr. Cervantes stated that such
  funds may be used for the maintenance, construction, and operation of
  public streets. In this instance, the funds are being used to install signage
  for the Preferential Parking District.

  Chief Manny Arana addressed concerns about police response, stating
  officers do respond, citations are issued, and records can be shared with
  residents. He also clarified that Council parking permits only apply to the
  city hall lot.

  Vice Mayor Rios recognizes that certain residences lack driveways.

  Mr. Houston reported that Mr. Cervantes noted the limited availability of
  real estate along the street. He observed that certain residences lack
  garages, while others have converted their garages into accessory dwelling
  units (ADUs).

  Council Member Davila inquired of Mr. Cervantes regarding the number
  of handicap spaces available on Beaudine, and whether the city provides
  additional permits to residents who possess a handicap placard.

  Mr. Cervantes stated that each property in the preferential parking district
  is eligible for two permits. He was unsure of the number of ADA spaces
  on Beaudine.

  Page 6 of 26
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 24, 2026

2
PARKING & TRAFFIC
CONT’D  Mr. Houston inquired whether possession of a handicap placard
  supersedes the municipality's authority to issue citations for parking
  without a street permit.

  Chief Arana confirmed that the handicap placard is not affected by the
  city’s program.

  Council Member Hurtado recognizes parking concerns, having previously
  lived without a driveway on Jackson. He is aware of the nearby college
  and apartment complex near Beaudine. Once signatures are verified, the
  council must proceed.

  Council Member Avalos noted the initial $1,500 cost from the gas tax and
  asked about the permit price for residents.

  Mr. Cervantes explained the police department manages the permit
  program.

  Mr. Cervantes and Chief Arana estimated each annual parking permit cost
  about $60.

  Council Member Avalos asked how much revenue the police department's
  16 extra permits will generate, and if the $1,500 will be reimbursed to the
  general fund or gas tax fund.

  Mr. Cervantes stated that the gas tax comprises funds received by the city
  on an annual basis. The city is entitled to allocate these funds at its
  discretion. Once the funds have been expended, there is no obligation for
  reimbursement. Therefore, even if the gas tax is used for initiatives that
  generate revenue for the general fund, reimbursement is not required.

  Council Member Avalos asked about the revenue, which is estimated at
  around $4,300 for the general fund. This will generate income for the city.

  Mr. Cervantes explained that the permit program's fees were intended to
  cover police department operating costs.

  Council Member Hurtado requested clarification regarding the permissible
  uses of the gas tax, noting that it cannot be used at discretion as previously
  assumed.

  Mr. Cervantes stated that gas tax funds can support any public right-of-
  way project, such as street signage.

  Page 7 of 26
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 24, 2026
2
PARKING & TRAFFIC
CONT’D  Vice Mayor Rios asked if Beaudine residents were involved.

  Mr. Cervantes clarified that the Council is considering this matter due to a
  petition submitted by those residents. Staff verifies the petition was
  approved by residents from each property; if two-thirds support it, the
  request goes to Council.

  Vice Mayor Rios inquired about the existence of an appeal process.

  Mr. Cervantes responded that he was not aware of any formal appeal
  procedure. However, residents have the option to request the removal of
  the preferential parking district within two years after its implementation,
  but this requires a vote among the residents.

  Council Member Avalos inquired about applying for extra permits.

  Chief Arana clarified each property is allowed two permits.

  Mr. Cervantes described the event parking rules for the preferential
  district.

  Council Member Hurtado motioned to approve this item and seconded by
  Council Member Davila.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Council Member Davila, yes; Vice Mayor Rios, yes; Mayor Barron,
  recused.
3
MUNICIPAL CODE ADMIN /
ENERGY AND CONSERVATION
PROGRAMS  Following the conclusion of the Public Hearing, the City Council
  unanimously approved items A & B by motion of Council Member Avalos
  and seconded by Vice Mayor Rios:

  a. Introduced Ordinance No. 2026-03-CC entitled Ordinance of the City
  Council of the City of South Gate, California, amending Title 9
  (Buildings) of the South Gate Municipal Code by adding new Chapter
  9.14 (Streamlined Permitting Process for Electric Vehicle Charging
  Stations), consistent with California Government Code Section
  65850.7 (AB 1236); and

  b. Finding that the proposed addition to the South Gate Municipal Code
  adds provisions that are administrative in nature, do not approve any
  physical development, and do not have the potential to result in
  individually or cumulatively significant effects on the environment,
  and therefore, the passage of this ordinance is exempt from California

  Page 8 of 26
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 24, 2026

3
MUNICIPAL CODE ADMIN /
ENERGY AND CONSERVATION
PROGRAMS CONT’D  Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA") review under the General Rule
  that CEQA only applies to projects with the potential to cause a
  significant effect on the environment and thus no environmental
  analysis or review is necessary- CEQA Guidelines Section
  15061(b)(3). The City Clerk is directed to file a Notice of Exemption
  with the County Clerk within five (5) working days of adoption.

  Mayor Barron asked if anyone in the audience wished to speak on this
  item.

  Mario Dominguez watched a Bell Gardens City Council meeting where a
  proposed development included a recommendation for the developer to
  add charging stations.

  Liz Ruiz, Kauffman Ave. asked whether city code discourages non-
  charging vehicles from parking at charging stations.

  Nibil Huzu, owner of Packtrack, aims to lead fleet electrification and
  promote renewable energy in South Gate.

  John Cataldo, an experienced architect in South Gate, designed the new
  facility recently described by Nibil. He expressed gratitude to the planning
  department for their assistance with the CUP application and urged the
  council to support streamlining this process. He emphasized that the
  proposed facility would be a valuable asset to both the state and the city,
  setting a precedent for renewable energy innovation, as it will utilize solar
  power to help electrify vehicles.

  Having no one else come forward, Mayor Barron closed the audience
  portion.

  Council Member Avalos inquired about the current permit application fee
  for an EV charging station installed on a residential property.

  John Signo, the Planning Manager, indicated that the planning review fee
  for architectural review is $563, which is collected for all stations.

  Council Member Avalos inquired about systems to ensure thorough
  application review while complying with state guidelines.

  Mr. Signo explained that the city must provide a checklist for applicants.
  The procedure is ministerial, skipping the planning process and going
  straight to Building and Safety, which conducts an administrative review.

  Page 9 of 26
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 24, 2026
3
MUNICIPAL CODE ADMIN /
ENERGY AND CONSERVATION
PROGRAMS CONT’D  Council Member Avalos noted a $563 fiscal impact and questioned if
  further fees would be collected for extra work, or if that amount is final.

  Mr. Signo replied that additional fees will be collected during the building
  and safety stage.

  Council Member Avalos asked how this ordinance would help the city
  compete for state or regional EV funding.

  Mr. Signo replied that compliance with state or federal requirements
  improves the city's chances of securing grants.

  Council Member Hurtado noted that this was passed in 2015 with a
  compliance deadline of 2017 and asked how oversight is managed for
  home vehicle charging to meet Assembly Bill 1236’s requirements.

  Mr. Signo explained that building and safety requires a ministerial,
  expedited permit for this process.

  Council Member Hurtado observed vehicles charging and left unattended,
  including at city hall stations.

  Mr. Houston clarified that installation and management are separate
  issues. This item concerns installation and permitting, such as at Tesla
  centers like Cross Roads Plaza, where Tesla regulates charging and
  parking enforcement.

  He noted a grant funded the city hall charging stations for free use, but
  staff believe the free period has ended. They are considering adding a
  system to charge fees if a fully charged car remains parked.

  Vice Mayor Rios and Mayor Barron support streamlining processes,
  particularly for electric vehicle charging stations.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Council Member Davila, yes; Vice Mayor Rios, yes; Mayor Barron,
  yes.

RECESS  The City Council recessed at 8:11 p.m., and reconvened at 8:18 p.m., with
  all Members of Council present.

  Page 10 of 26
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 24, 2026

PRESENTATION

4
BUDGET ADMIN  The City Council unanimously received and filed a presentation on Budget
  Reduction from Administrative Services, Police Department, Human
  Resources, and Public Works Department by motion of Council Member
  Davila and seconded by Council Member Avalos.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Council Member Davila, yes; Vice Mayor Rios, yes; Mayor Barron,
  yes.

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
